title: Sesame-Ginger Chicken Cucumber Rice Bowls
dek: Juicy sliced chicken, cool cucumber, jammy eggs, and a glossy sesame-ginger sauce over hot rice.
image_alt: Sesame chicken and vegetables served beside steamed rice
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, sliced into thin cutlets
1 English cucumber, diced or thinly sliced

instructions.name: Make the sauce
instructions.text: Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic.

instructions.name: Sear the chicken
instructions.text: Pat chicken dry. Sear in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until browned and 165°F.

instructions.name: Glaze
instructions.text: Lower heat and add half the sauce. Turn the chicken until glossy, then rest 5 minutes and slice.

instructions.name: Season the cucumber
instructions.text: Toss cucumber with 1 tablespoon of the remaining sauce and a pinch of salt.

instructions.name: Build the bowls
instructions.text: Divide rice among bowls and add chicken, cucumber, egg, scallions, sesame seeds, and the remaining sauce.

why_it_works: Thin cutlets brown before they dry out.
A separate cucumber seasoning keeps the bowl fresh instead of uniformly sweet.
Warm rice and cool toppings give the bowl restaurant-style contrast.
swaps: Use boneless thighs for extra richness.
Swap rice for soba noodles or quinoa.
Use edamame instead of eggs for a dairy-free, egg-free variation.
storage: Refrigerate chicken, rice, and cucumber separately up to 4 days. Reheat chicken and rice before adding cold toppings.
notes: Do not pour all the sauce into the skillet; the clean reserved portion is for serving.
Toast sesame seeds briefly in a dry skillet for stronger flavor.

faqs.a: Yes. Keep cucumber and eggs separate from the hot components until serving.
Yes. Brown it well, then stir in half the sauce and serve it over rice.
It is not spicy. Add chili crisp or sriracha at the table if you want heat.

title: Spicy Pancetta Vodka Rigatoni
dek: Silky tomato-cream rigatoni with crisp pancetta, chile heat, Parmesan, and basil—the weeknight pasta that feels like going out.
image_alt: Rigatoni coated in a glossy spicy tomato sauce with basil

instructions.name: Boil the pasta
instructions.text: Cook rigatoni in salted water until 1 minute shy of al dente. Reserve 1 1/2 cups pasta water.

instructions.name: Crisp the pancetta
instructions.text: Cook pancetta in a wide skillet until browned. Transfer half to a paper towel and leave the rendered fat in the pan.

instructions.name: Build the sauce
instructions.text: Add garlic, red pepper flakes, and tomato paste. Cook until the paste turns brick red, then add vodka and simmer 1 minute.

instructions.name: Make it silky
instructions.text: Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 6 minutes. Lower heat and stir in cream, Parmesan, and 1/2 cup pasta water.

instructions.name: Finish
instructions.text: Add rigatoni and toss until glossy. Fold in basil and top with the reserved crisp pancetta.

why_it_works: Browning tomato paste removes raw acidity and deepens flavor.
Pasta water binds tomato, cream, and cheese into one sauce.
Holding back some pancetta preserves crisp texture.
swaps: Use bacon if pancetta is unavailable.
Replace vodka with chicken broth plus 1 teaspoon lemon juice at the end.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water or milk.
notes: Keep the sauce below a hard boil after adding cream.
Grate Parmesan finely so it melts without clumping.

faqs.a: No. It cooks down and mainly helps carry aromatic tomato flavor.
Yes. Omit pancetta and start with 2 tablespoons olive oil plus a pinch of smoked paprika.

faqs.q: Can I make it less spicy?
faqs.a: Cut the red pepper flakes to a pinch or omit them entirely.

title: Miso-Maple Salmon Rice Bowls
dek: Caramelized miso-maple salmon with avocado, cucumber, edamame, and a sharp sesame-lime drizzle.
image_alt: Miso salmon rice bowl with avocado cucumber and edamame
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb salmon fillet, cut into 4 portions

instructions.name: Mix the glaze
instructions.text: Whisk miso, maple syrup, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil until smooth.

instructions.name: Glaze the salmon
instructions.text: Pat salmon dry and brush generously with two-thirds of the glaze.

instructions.name: Roast
instructions.text: Roast at 425°F for 10 to 14 minutes, brushing once more near the end, until the center flakes easily.

instructions.name: Make the drizzle
instructions.text: Stir remaining glaze with 1 tablespoon lime juice and 1 tablespoon warm water.

instructions.name: Assemble
instructions.text: Divide rice, avocado, cucumber, and edamame among bowls. Add salmon and finish with drizzle, scallions, sesame seeds, and lime.

why_it_works: Miso adds savory depth that balances maple sweetness.
High oven heat caramelizes the glaze without a long marinade.
Cool cucumber and avocado offset the rich salmon.
swaps: Swap rice for quinoa or cauliflower rice.
Add shredded cabbage for extra crunch.
storage: Refrigerate components separately up to 3 days. Reheat salmon gently or serve it cold.
notes: Miso and soy sauce are salty; taste before adding extra salt.
Do not overcook salmon—the glaze will continue darkening after the fish is done.

faqs.q: Can I air fry the salmon?
faqs.a: Yes. Air fry at 400°F for about 8 to 10 minutes depending on thickness.
No need. Thirty minutes is plenty; long miso marinades can make the surface overly salty.
No. Add chili crisp if you want heat.

title: Roasted Sweet Potato Ginger Soup
dek: Velvety roasted sweet potato soup with ginger, warm spices, lime, and crunchy pepitas.
image_alt: Creamy orange sweet potato soup with herbs and pepitas
ingredients: 2 lb sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed

instructions.name: Roast the vegetables
instructions.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potatoes, carrot, and onion with oil and a pinch of salt. Roast 25 to 30 minutes until deeply browned.

instructions.name: Bloom aromatics
instructions.text: Add ginger, garlic, cumin, and paprika to a soup pot with a teaspoon of oil and cook 45 seconds.

instructions.name: Simmer
instructions.text: Add roasted vegetables and broth. Simmer 8 minutes.

instructions.name: Blend
instructions.text: Blend until completely smooth, then stir in coconut milk.

instructions.name: Balance
instructions.text: Add lime juice, salt, and pepper. Serve with pepitas and herbs.

why_it_works: Roasting gives the soup sweetness and depth that boiling alone cannot.
Ginger and lime keep the sweet potato from tasting heavy.
Pepitas add the texture a puréed soup needs.
swaps: Use butternut squash for half the sweet potato.
Heavy cream can replace coconut milk.
Add a pinch of cayenne for heat.
storage: Refrigerate 5 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat gently and thin with broth if needed.
notes: Blend in batches if using a countertop blender and vent the lid.
Roast until the edges are dark; that browning matters.

faqs.a: It already is when made with vegetable broth and coconut milk.
Yes, but the flavor will be lighter. Simmer the vegetables until very tender.
Grilled cheese, a crisp salad, or toasted naan all work.
